summary.why_it_matters: This is the first large study describing pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest across Australia and New Zealand, showing that incidence, arrest features, and survival differ strongly by age and may need age-specific emergency care planning.
summary.design: Observational analysis of EMS-attended cardiac arrests in children under 18 years from 2017 to 2023, using registry data and logistic regression to examine predictors of survival.
summary.key_findings: EMS attended 4,779 cases and treated 3,139 (65.7%). Incidence was 10.1 per 100,000 person-years for attended and 6.6 for treated cases, with peaks in infants (65.4) and adolescents (11.4). summary.bottom_line: Age-specific prevention and resuscitation strategies are needed because pediatric arrest patterns and outcomes vary substantially across developmental stages.

papers.methods_note: Multinational EMS registry cohort (Aus-ROC Epistry) with multivariable logistic regression.
